question: Approve the ideation direction: a binary-side fail-closed boot receipt checked against the durable compact_boundary record, with no hook?

artifacts.summary: Ran a live capture spike on Claude Code 2.1.226 and disproved BOTH options the seed proposed. The hook is rejected on necessity: PreCompact fired on a /compact the host then REFUSED ('Not enough messages to compact'), so it false-positives, and it produced nothing at the incident boundary. The naive session-identity tell is disproven by capture: session_id is identical across PreCompact, SessionStart(source:compact), and the boundary — identity survives compaction. What does work is a durable timestamped compact_boundary transcript record, captured for the spike session AND for this session's own incident boundary (fedfe9c3, 18:59:30Z, 801920 to 19650 tokens). Design: status --boot writes a per-session receipt; FO-held mutating verbs refuse until the receipt postdates the latest boundary. No hook, no escape hatch, honest fail-open degradation on non-Claude hosts. Surface net +540 across ~12 files (+560/-20), tolerance 2x net; product +145, tests +340 (first instinct ~170, explicitly doubled per today's calibration), docs +55.
